title: Getting started with BamScale
text: BamScale provides multithreaded sequential BAM traversal R/Bioconductor workflows. package designed users already rely Rsamtools, GenomicAlignments, BiocParallel, need faster BAM parsing without moving separate non-Bioconductor workflow model. package targets three common classes BAM access: metadata-oriented scans filtering, fragment summaries, quality control generation alignment objects downstream GenomicAlignments workflows sequence quality extraction, including optimized compact mode motivation inclusion Bioconductor therefore straightforward: BamScale accelerates core data-access bottleneck preserving familiar Bioconductor inputs, filtering semantics, output types.

title: Getting started with BamScale
text: BamScale intended complement, replace, existing Bioconductor packages. Rsamtools remains canonical low-level BAM access layer R defines filtering idioms BamScale reuses ScanBamParam. GenomicAlignments remains standard package alignment-centric downstream workflows, BamScale supports direct generation compatible alignment objects. BiocParallel remains standard mechanism file-level parallelism, BamScale adds second axis parallelism per-file OpenMP threads. main difference therefore performance-oriented: BamScale accelerates traversal step staying close existing Bioconductor usage patterns.

title: Benchmarking BamScale: reader throughput and end-to-end workflow impact
text: BamScale multithreaded BAM reader, built ompBAM OpenMP engine, returns native Bioconductor objects standard readers drop-replacement Rsamtools::scanBam GenomicAlignments::readGAlignments. Reading BAM one step analysis, faster reader speeds workflow end--end proportion time workflow spends reading (Amdahl’s law). vignette summarises benchmarks quantify raw read speedup end--end effect two standard workflows — coverage/bigWig track generation ATAC-seq fragment-size QC — BamScale output verified byte-identical standard tools. numbers concise summary representative benchmark run (Intel Xeon Gold 6252, 96 cores; warm page cache; median 5 iterations). benchmark harness produces inst/benchmarks/ (run_server_benchmark.R, run_workflow_benchmark.R); see last section reproduce full results.

title: Benchmarking BamScale: reader throughput and end-to-end workflow impact
text: single large BAM, BamScale reads 2.5–4x faster standard reader across three representative access patterns, spreads BGZF decode across cores assembles output objects native code: Single-file read throughput: best BamScale configuration vs single-threaded standard reader (median 5 iterations).  Two honest points. one thread BamScale modestly faster single-threaded readers (1.1–1.3x, native-code object assembly); win comes threading, scaling strongly sublinear – roughly 2.5–4x 48 threads, largely saturating 24 48 threads. value near-linear scaling ability use cores single-threaded reader use – one large BAM interactive session. Object-free command-line decoders samtools reach several-fold higher raw throughput, return Bioconductor object; BamScale’s role fast, object-faithful decoding inside R.

Read-pattern rows single-file read throughput; workflow rows end--end. Read fraction share standard pipeline spent reading.  ATAC fragment-size QC nearly pure read, BamScale’s read speedup carries almost intact: 4.14x end--end. Coverage -> bigWig dominated shared, single-threaded rtracklayer::export.bw step (identical work arms), end--end gain bounded 1.24x even though read phase 6.6x faster. Stopping -memory coverage RleList – many analyses consume next – recovers 3.29x gain. (Since 0.99.14, bam_coverage() bam_coverage_bigwig() compute endpoints directly inside reader, removing R-side read phase entirely; see function documentation.)

code: library(BamScale)  bam <- ompBAM::example_BAM("Unsorted")  # Core alignment fields (scanBam-style extraction) x <- bam_read(   bam,   what    = c("qname", "flag", "rname", "pos", "mapq", "cigar"),   threads = 4 )  # A GAlignments object (drop-in for readGAlignments) ga <- bam_read(   bam,   what    = c("rname", "pos", "cigar", "strand"),   as      = "GAlignments",   threads = 4 )  # Sequence + base quality, in standard-compatible objects sq <- bam_read(   bam,   what         = c("qname", "seq", "qual"),   seqqual_mode = "compatible",   threads      = 4 )  # Fast chromosome-level counts cnt <- bam_count(bam, threads = 4)  # In-reader aggregation (0.99.14): summaries computed inside the C++ reader, # byte-identical to the scanBam/coverage equivalents fs  <- fragment_sizes(bam, threads = 4)   # paired-end fragment-size distribution mq  <- mapq_dist(bam, threads = 4)        # mapping-quality distribution cov <- bam_coverage(bam, threads = 4)     # per-base coverage RleList bam_coverage_bigwig(bam, "coverage.bw", threads = 4)  # single-pass BAM -> bigWig

title: Bioconductor-Friendly Multithreaded BAM Processing
text: BamScale fits Rsamtools GenomicAlignments already fit, adding within-file threading axis top: Field extraction via = c("qname", "flag", "rname", "pos", "mapq", "cigar", ...) — metadata pattern behind QC, filtering, fragment-level summaries. Alignment objects via = "GAlignments" = "GAlignmentPairs". scanBam-shaped lists via = "scanBam", data.frame / S4Vectors::DataFrame. ScanBamParam-style filtering: mapqFilter, flag, , , tag. File-level parallelism via BiocParallel (BPPARAM), exactly standard workflow.

title: Bioconductor-Friendly Multithreaded BAM Processing
text: BamScale parallelizes two axes — across files via BPPARAM workers, within file via OpenMP threads. Approximate effective concurrency: auto_threads = TRUE, BamScale keeps per-file thread counts high possible — reducing number concurrently active file workers shrinks per-file threads. Within-file threading key difference baseline model, reason BamScale removes read bottleneck fewer files cores.

title: Fast BAM reading with Bioconductor-compatible arguments — bam_read
text: bam_read() intentionally column-compatible common BAM fields used Bioconductor workflows can used fast drop-reader conversion downstream classes. Parallelism model: BPPARAM parallelizes across files (one file per BiocParallel worker). threads parallelizes within file via OpenMP. Effective total concurrency approximately min(length(file), BiocParallel::bpnworkers(BPPARAM)) * threads. auto_threads = TRUE BPPARAM multiple workers, BamScale first limits number concurrently active workers preserve requested per-file thread count within detected core budget, caps per-file OpenMP threads single file still oversubscribe machine. Compatibility notes: rname, mrnm, strand returned factor columns, matching Rsamtools::scanBam(). rname/mrnm levels BAM header reference names; unmapped unset references NA ("*"). strand levels c("+", "-", "*"). Region filtering via param$supported sequential filter (index-jump random access). Flag filtering uses ScanBamFlag semantics converting logical flag requirements required-set required-unset bit masks. Tag values returned native BAM-derived type, matching scanBam(): integer-valued tags (c, C, s, S, , ) become integer columns (double value exceeds R integer range), floating-point (f) tags become double columns, /Z/H/B tags become character columns. B tags comma-separated character values. Absent tag values NA. seqqual_mode = "compact" optimized throughput-oriented benchmarking returns raw list-columns seq/qual, ordinary sequence quality strings. representation, seq contains BAM-packed nucleotide bytes qual contains raw Phred bytes. Compact output intended users want defer avoid full string-materialization costs; use decode_compact_seq(), decode_compact_qual(), decode_seqqual_compact() decode compact output back standard string form needed. "GAlignments" "GAlignmentPairs" output exclude unmapped records. = "scanBam" returns strict scan-like list--lists: without param$, returns one unnamed batch; param$, returns one batch per range label (including empty ranges), requested fields tag values $tag. output mode, seq qual returned Biostrings::DNAStringSet Biostrings::PhredQuality closer scanBam() compatibility.

title: BamScale 0.99.14
text: fragment_sizes(): paired-end fragment-size (insert-size) distribution; identical table(abs(scanBam(isize))). drop_mate_unmapped = TRUE (default) replicates scanBam’s isize = NA rule mate-unmapped reads. mapq_dist(): mapping-quality distribution; identical table(scanBam(mapq)) (MAPQ 255 reported 255, scanBam uses NA). bam_coverage(): per-base coverage SimpleRleList; identical() GenomicAlignments::coverage(readGAlignments(...)), including CIGAR conventions (M/=/X/D cover, N gaps, drop.D.ranges = FALSE) readGAlignments record filter (unmapped reads dropped). bam_coverage_bigwig(): single-pass BAM -> coverage bigWig written natively via bundled libBigWig – R-side coverage object, rtracklayer::export.bw round-trip. Data zoom blocks compressed across OpenMP threads (parallel = TRUE, default); parallel output bit--bit identical serial writer. compress_level argument exposes zlib deflate level, verbose = TRUE prints per-phase timing breakdown. bam_read(= "GAlignments") now uses dedicated fast path assembles GAlignments slots C++: seqnames/strand accumulated run-length pairs inside parallel region, cigar column materialised CHARSXP cache exploits CIGAR-string redundancy, qname decoded actually requested. Output identical() GenomicAlignments::readGAlignments() (verified 226M-read scale) previous construction path. options(BamScale.ga_fastpath = FALSE) restores old path. Vendored libBigWig 0.4.8 (MIT, Devon Ryan) src/libBigWig/ (built -DNOCURL, local files ). Local modifications, commented bwWrite.c: tunable zlib deflate level, deferred parallel block compression, zoom-level construction -memory coverage runs instead re-reading just-written data section.

title: BamScale 0.99.14
text: Fixed quadratic reallocation pattern reader’s batch merge: per-batch exact-capacity reserve() calls copied accumulated data every batch. Buffers now grow geometrically. affects every read path – e.g. 229M-read BAM 48 threads, = "GAlignments" dropped ~300 s ~56 s, plain data-frame reads improved 2.8-4.4x. CIGAR strings formatted allocation-free digit writer instead per-op std::to_string. Representative large-file results (229M-read ATAC BAM, 48 threads, warm cache): bam_coverage() 7.2x vs coverage(readGAlignments()); bam_coverage_bigwig() 2.6x vs megadepth equal compression; fragment_sizes() 5.4x vs scanBam + table(); = "GAlignments" 4.8x vs readGAlignments() (faster even single-threaded).

title: BamScale 0.99.14
text: Removed long-standing ^src/Makevars$ entry .Rbuildignore (dating pkgdown setup): built tarballs – including Bioconductor builds – shipped without src/Makevars therefore compiled WITHOUT OpenMP (without explicit -lz), silently running single-threaded installed tarball. -place R CMD INSTALL . unaffected, local installs always threaded. Tarball builds now carry full build configuration (OpenMP, zlib, -DNOCURL, bundled libBigWig objects).

title: BamScale 0.99.14
text: run_workflow_benchmark.R gains first-class arms four new functions (--include-fastcov/-bigwig/-fragsize/-mapq), behind identical() correctness gate, optional megadepth context arm (--megadepth-bin). run_server_benchmark.R: BiocParallel PSOCK clusters now started namespaces pre-loaded outside timed region multi-file arms (previously cluster spin-charged every iteration, diluting comparator ratios high worker counts); added --include-single single multi scenarios can run separate stages. New reproducible manuscript-benchmark tooling: select_encode_atac.R (ENCODE portal selection -> accession/md5 manifest), manifest-driven download_atac_data.R md5 verification, samtools_reference.sh, merge_runs.R, staged run_manuscript_final.sh orchestrator.

title: BamScale 0.99.14
